findings.summary: Reuse the shared numeric binding-scope restoration in geometry and CSM adapters; retain only CSM's distinct symbol-map restoration.
Reuse lowerTupleComponents for both pinned geometry index-pair paths rather than duplicating tuple validation and component lowering.
Remove the duplicate static-unrolled-iteration stack and use completion frames for both lifetime and frame-yield membership.
Check root and alias membership before type-querying mutation-scan initializers, avoiding unrelated TypeChecker work.
Dispatch gizmo placement through resolved binding identity instead of recognizing emitted C++ receiver prefixes.
Move ordinary continue and bounded scalar chained-assignment syntax into the shared numeric statement lowerer.
Share checked PBR output identity and local-alias resolution between GPU transport and CPU normalization projections.
Hoist the duplicated nullable pinned-handle/material classification and reuse it across resource-loop analyses.
Use append-only particle construction and bake-request counts in loop snapshots instead of repeatedly serializing and hashing graph documents.
Traverse scoped values during collection assignment only when an actual cardinality taint request requires invalidation.
Count instantiated glTF primitives directly from the validated mesh instead of wrapping it in a synthetic one-mesh document.
Derive native field argument spellings from the validated field values instead of maintaining a second synchronized array.
Represent construction checkpoint counters and ordered light identities explicitly instead of interpreting a mixed positional array.
Reuse commonResourceValue when merging runtime mesh-template capabilities while retaining explicit identity stripping.
Skip non-ShaderMaterial mesh rows before allocating candidate-variant sets during thin-instance settlement.
Emit the identity-guarded default render graph once through the existing native-function registry instead of repeating its constructors at every task or registration site.
